hints.title: Mark the two choices
hints.body: Underline “every” and “some”. For each word, identify exactly which numbers it refers to.
hints.recap: The order of “every” and “some” matters: a later choice may depend on an earlier one.
hints.pitfall: Keep “factor of n greater than one” as the domain for m.
hints.pause: Write the claim about a factor first, then the claim about a member of S.

recall.reminder: The order of “every” and “some” matters: a later choice may depend on an earlier one.

hints.title: Negate one layer at a time
hints.body: To negate “every object has property P”, look for an object where P fails. To negate “some object has property Q”, require Q to fail for every object in that domain.
hints.recap: Negate the quantified claim while keeping the domains unchanged.
hints.pitfall: Do not reverse which number divides which.
hints.pause: Apply the rules to your statement, then express its negation in the wording of the options.

recall.reminder: Negate the quantified claim while keeping the domains unchanged.

solution:
Failure means there is at least one factor m of n with m>1 for which no member of S divides m. Equivalently, that factor is not a multiple of any member of S.

The outer every becomes there exists, and the inner some becomes none. The eligible factors and the direction of divisibility stay unchanged. Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Negate nested forall-exists while retaining domain
